# Artifact Keeper 1.11.11

A maintenance release on the 1.11 line: 9 changelog entries from 9 pull requests since 1.11.10, all landed on `main` first and brought to the line in #5102, #5104, #5106, #5116, #5120, #5122, #5124, #5125 and #5172. Two fix problems users reported: **SSO and CI OIDC requests now send a User-Agent and report the identity provider's HTTP status** (#5036, in #5114), so an OIDC login behind a web application firewall no longer fails with an invalid JSON error, and **the npm version route resolves dist-tags such as `latest`** (#5063, in #5113). Four tighten what a Remote or an inspect route may reach: **IP-literal upstream destinations are checked against the outbound address policy in every egress routing mode** (#5095, in #5100), **OCI scan-on-proxy withholds a manifest it cannot classify under `fail_closed`** (#5097, in #5099), and **image inspect resolves a digest, its config and its provenance only within the requested repository and image** (#5096 and #5111, in #5098 and #5112). **Google Cloud Storage error messages no longer carry the request URL** (#5093, in #5094), **libz-sys moves to 1.1.31** for RUSTSEC-2026-0418 (#5107, in #5108), and **wasmtime moves to 36.0.20 and pulldown-cmark to 0.13.6** for RUSTSEC-2026-0424 and RUSTSEC-2026-0433, with RUSTSEC-2026-0429 ignored on a build-time zip (#5162, in #5164). **No schema migrations** (the line stays at migration 289), no new settings, and the scanner adapter stays at 1.5.2.

## What changed

- **SSO and CI OIDC requests send a User-Agent and report identity-provider HTTP errors** (#5036, in #5114). Requests to identity providers (SSO discovery, token, JWKS and userinfo; CI OIDC discovery and JWKS) carry `User-Agent: artifact-keeper/<version>`, so a web application firewall that refuses requests without one, such as the AWS WAF core rule set, no longer blocks them. A non-2xx answer from discovery or JWKS is logged as `returned HTTP <status>` instead of an invalid JSON error, and so is a non-JSON token endpoint error. Login responses still show only a generic error.
- **npm: the version route resolves dist-tags** (#5063, in #5113). `GET /npm/{repo}/{package}/{version}` answered 404 for a dist-tag such as `latest` or `next` on Local, Remote and Virtual repositories. The segment now resolves through the package's `dist-tags` when no version of that name exists, as the npm registry does. On an age-gated Remote or Virtual repository a tag resolves through the gated `dist-tags`, so `latest` names the newest version old enough to download.
- **Google Cloud Storage error messages no longer carry the request URL** (#5093, in #5094). A GCS transport failure used to repeat the full request URL, naming the endpoint host, the bucket and the object key, in the storage error, the `/health` storage check and API error bodies. They now name only the operation and the transport error, as 1.11.4 did for Azure. A few S3 error paths are trimmed the same way, and the health check strips any URL left in a backend's message.
- **A Remote applies the upstream outbound address policy to IP-literal destinations in every egress routing mode** (#5095, in #5100). URLs a Remote reads from upstream content, such as chart URLs in a Helm `index.yaml`, were checked against the policy only when the repository routed through an explicit egress proxy; with direct or inherited routing an IP-literal host never reached the resolver check. Every upstream fetch now checks an IP-literal destination (numeric, octal and hex IPv4 spellings, IPv6, IPv4-mapped and NAT64 addresses) before sending, and a refused destination answers `502` with `UPSTREAM_DESTINATION_REFUSED`. The private-CIDR allowlist and `UPSTREAM_ALLOW_PRIVATE_IPS` apply as they do when an upstream URL is saved. The VS Code gallery query now goes through the repository's egress routing, and the CI OIDC token exchange checks the JWKS URL the issuer's discovery document names.
- **Image inspect and base-image info resolve a digest only within the requested repository and image** (#5096, in #5098). A `sha256:` reference used to be read as given, so on storage shared by several repositories the routes could describe a manifest stored for another repository or image. A digest now resolves only when a tag of the image names it, the image's catalog records it, or the repository holds it as a child of an index that belongs to the image. Any other digest answers like one that does not exist. Inspecting a Virtual repository by digest now answers 404, as by tag already did.
- **OCI scan-on-proxy withholds a manifest it cannot classify under `fail_closed`** (#5097, in #5099). The inline scan gate on a Remote OCI repository skipped every manifest it did not recognise as a runnable image, including ones it could not parse. The gate now classifies positively: a manifest skips the scan only when no container runtime would run it (an index, an artifact manifest, no config, no layers, or no layer a runtime would unpack, which covers Helm charts, cosign signatures, SBOMs, WASM and Flux artifacts). A manifest that does not parse, uses case-variant or duplicate field names, or pairs an unrecognised config with an unpackable layer is handled like an inconclusive scan: `423` under `fail_closed`, served `pending` under `fail_open` and record-only, and counted under a new `unclassifiable` verdict label. A Remote member served through a Virtual repository now also refuses Docker schema1 manifests under scan-on-proxy.
- **Image inspect reads config and provenance only from the requesting repository** (#5111, in #5112). The config blob and the provenance attestation layer a manifest names were read by digest alone. Both are now read only when the repository records them, as its hosted blob downloads require; an unrecorded config answers like a missing one and unrecorded provenance is left out. A missing object's 404 message no longer carries the storage backend's error text.
- **libz-sys moved to 1.1.31 for RUSTSEC-2026-0418** (#5107, in #5108). The advisory concerns the crate's build script output when built with `cc` 1.6.0 or later; the backend builds with `cc` 1.2.55, so this clears the audit finding rather than a runtime exposure.
- **wasmtime moved to 36.0.20 for RUSTSEC-2026-0424, pulldown-cmark to 0.13.6 for RUSTSEC-2026-0433, and RUSTSEC-2026-0429 ignored on utoipa-swagger-ui's build-time zip** (#5162, in #5164). The wasmtime advisory lets a component that receives a borrow of a resource it defines itself grow host memory that is never charged to the store, so an installed plugin could have exhausted backend memory; installing a plugin requires an administrator. pulldown-cmark is a build-time dependency and is not linked into the backend. zip 2.4.2 is only a build dependency of utoipa-swagger-ui, whose build script never calls `ZipArchive::extract`; the backend's own zip is 9.x.

## Upgrade notes

There is no migration and no new or changed setting. Behaviours operators may notice:

- A Remote whose stored upstream URL is a private IP literal, saved before upstream URLs were validated, stops fetching until that address is admitted by the private-CIDR allowlist or `UPSTREAM_ALLOW_PRIVATE_IPS`. A loopback or link-local upstream (a sidecar mirror on `127.0.0.1`, for example) cannot be admitted; point it at a non-loopback address. When the CIDR allowlist is set, it takes precedence over `UPSTREAM_ALLOW_PRIVATE_IPS` for upstream fetches, as it already did when saving an upstream URL.
- On a Remote OCI repository with scan-on-proxy and `fail_closed`, an artifact that pairs its own config with OCI image layers (a BuildKit registry cache exported with `image-manifest=true`, or an artifact pushed by older ORAS releases with `application/vnd.unknown.config.v1+json` over `application/vnd.oci.image.layer.v1.tar`) is now withheld with `423`. Proxy such artifacts through a Remote without scan-on-proxy, or with `fail_open`. Dashboards or alerts that enumerate the verdict label of the proxy scan verdict metric should add `unclassifiable`.
- `image-inspect` and `image-builds/base-info` answer 404 (or `found: false`) for a digest the requested repository and image do not record, where they used to describe it.
- SSO login failures caused by a non-2xx discovery, JWKS or token answer now appear in the server log with the HTTP status; the login response is unchanged.

The full entries are in the `## [1.11.11]` section of [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/artifact-keeper/artifact-keeper/blob/v1.11.11/CHANGELOG.md).
